project.purpose: Own authoritative interactive game products and game-specific research while keeping mechanics, lenses, teardowns, and experiments composable rather than turning one product's rules into universal Game law.

nodes.label: ProductAuthority
nodes.responsibility: Own the current executable product/ruleset identity and player-visible game semantics.
acceptance: Current executable and ruleset are explicit.

nodes.label: MechanismLibrary
nodes.responsibility: Retain source-grounded mechanics, relationships, tensions, and counterexamples as advisory reusable material.
acceptance: Retrieval returns evidence and conditions without blocking novel combinations.

nodes.label: ExperimentLane
nodes.responsibility: Run bounded playable or mechanical probes without silently promoting them to product direction.
acceptance: Experiment outcomes remain scoped to their hypothesis and evidence.

nodes.label: CompositionPlanner
nodes.responsibility: Compose product-native mechanics from optional lenses, mechanism evidence, and current product intent.
acceptance: A proposed composition names assumptions/falsifiers instead of claiming guaranteed fun.

nodes.label: PlayerEvidence
nodes.responsibility: Separate mechanical/agent checks from claims about human play experience.
acceptance: Human-response claims remain unobserved unless actual scoped evidence exists.

nodes.label: StatefulSessionKernel
nodes.responsibility: Own the bounded Causal Lag run state machine: persistent architecture/cause, delayed execution, cumulative contract standing, and session termination while accepting validated session-rule inputs.
nodes.replacementContract: A replacement must preserve the public state/transition semantics, default R3 four-round behavior, and fail-closed validation of supplied session rules.
acceptance: Default R3 session remains four rounds with target 320.
A validated external sessionRules contract can substitute the context path without forking the session engine.

nodes.label: ContentGrammarCompiler
nodes.responsibility: Own thin Causal Lag content-unit and run-recipe composition over existing contexts, validating exact seams and compiling recipes into session rules.
nodes.replacementContract: A replacement may change authoring representation but must preserve context-seam validation, target reachability checks, no reward/session authority, and R3-compatible compiled output.
acceptance: Content units contain only authored role plus existing source/execution context identities.
Adjacent units fail closed unless the execution/source context seam discharges.
One seven-beat recipe compiles into the verified StatefulSessionKernel.

nodes.label: BreadthVerifier
nodes.responsibility: Mechanically distinguish meaningful existing-mechanic content variation from nominal reskins by enumerating policy effects and bounded terminal witnesses.
nodes.replacementContract: A replacement must keep mechanical policy-diversity evidence separate from Human-value claims and retain explicit tested state-space bounds.
acceptance: The tested 3x3 transition space reports exact evaluated-state and policy-signature counts.
The representative arc retains both reachable success and mathematically unrecoverable failure.
No Human or product authority is minted.

edges.label: only admitted product composition changes product
stateful session trajectories and terminal outcomes

slices.objective: Use the mechanism/counterexample library to propose one bounded next product/mechanic experiment without promoting advisory patterns into design law.
acceptance: Proposal cites source-grounded mechanisms, states falsifiers, and remains separate from product selection until evidence exists.

slices.objective: Prove that Causal Lag can gain content breadth by composing existing context transitions into one stateful seven-beat arc without adding player verbs or duplicating the session kernel.
acceptance: Content-unit seams compose exactly and compile into R3-compatible session rules.
The existing 3x3 transition space yields multiple mechanically distinct policy signatures.
The seven-beat browser arc reaches both SUCCESS and unrecoverable FAILURE in deterministic witnesses.

gaps: R4 proves one seven-beat breadth arc but not a longer campaign/run topology or sustainable large-scale content production.
Pressure dimensions beyond context recombination remain deferred until existing breadth saturates or a concrete failure requires them.
Human comprehension, perceived difficulty, enjoyment, retention, and market value remain unobserved.

review.notes: Updated after the first prospective Game use of the current Ordivon LEGO theory stack. Only architecture-relevant responsibilities exposed by the verified R3/R4 implementation were added; theory lenses remain external analysis aids rather than project nodes.
